drivers.variant_notes: Oliver's 2004 free-play firmware for the same machine, replacing U2/U6 with skat2732.u2 and 7406fn.u6. The archive's info.txt enables free play with S25 and S26 both ON. PinMAME declares the same controller, display, sound and flipper topology, and the retained service test gives the same thirteen coil pairings.

drivers.description: Skateball (Improved attract mode, Free Play rev. 3)
drivers.variant_notes: Oliver's 2005 improved-attract/free-play revision 3 for the same machine, replacing U2/U6 with skate02.u2 and skate02.u6 and retaining the same 823-02_4.716 sound. PinMAME declares the same topology and the retained service test gives the same thirteen coil pairings; no edition hardware change is evidenced.

The game's switch-identification table and its own matrix wiring establish this contact. The MPU reads the switch matrix without complementing it; the table writes state 1 for a closure at the bound public switch address. The physical contact rests open, separately from PinMAME's informational inversion flag. Legacy evidence mislabelled public 1 as tilt and public 2 as a ball-roll tilt. The factory table leaves 1 blank, puts all three tilts at 7, and names 2 MIDDLE RIGHT DROP TARGET. The retained gameplay trace closes 3 and 4 then 2 and the ROM resets the middle bank at output 10 without tilting.

mechanisms.behavior: 5 independently latched drop targets; each down contact remains closed until the shared reset coil at public 8 raises the bank. The script maps the target-down addresses 20, 21, 22, 23, 24 individually and raises all together on that output. Start/reset actions come from the ROM; do not substitute an all-down software timer. The three extra hit-scoring contacts on shared switch 17 are separate from these latched contacts; see the recreation note for their fitment.
mechanisms.label: Five-target SKATE bank

mechanisms.behavior: 3 independently latched drop targets; each down contact remains closed until the shared reset coil at public 9 raises the bank. The script maps the target-down addresses 26, 27, 28 individually and raises all together on that output. Start/reset actions come from the ROM; do not substitute an all-down software timer. The three extra hit-scoring contacts on shared switch 17 are separate from these latched contacts; see the recreation note for their fitment.
mechanisms.label: Top three-target bank

mechanisms.behavior: 3 independently latched drop targets; each down contact remains closed until the shared reset coil at public 10 raises the bank. The script maps the target-down addresses 2, 3, 4 individually and raises all together on that output. Start/reset actions come from the ROM; do not substitute an all-down software timer. The three extra hit-scoring contacts on shared switch 17 are separate from these latched contacts; see the recreation note for their fitment.
mechanisms.label: Middle three-target bank

mechanisms.behavior: One ball rests in the outhole at startup, closing 8. Output 7 kicks it toward the shooter lane and the switch opens as the ball leaves. The manual shooter then launches it; no shooter switch, multiball trough stack or ball lock is evidenced.
mechanisms.label: Single-ball outhole and serve

mechanisms.behavior: A ball entering the saucer closes 5 and remains captured while the ROM scores its award or bonus. Output 2 ejects it back onto the playfield; open 5 when the ball leaves. The retained embedded script aims about 195 degrees at force 20 VPX units; these are implementation tuning clues, not measured factory timing or force.
mechanisms.label: Saucer kickout

mechanisms.behavior: Each skirt closure requests its own thumper coil: left 40 to 11, bottom 39 to 12, right 38 to 13. The ball is repelled by the ring and the skirt contact opens again; no home-position sensor exists.
mechanisms.label: Three thumper bumpers

mechanisms.behavior: The left rebound contacts at 37 request coil 14; the right contacts at 36 request coil 15. A kick moves the rubber arm then springs back. The factory table explicitly says the sling and thumper coils energize when their switch is made.
mechanisms.label: Two slingshots

mechanisms.behavior: Each cabinet button powers both flippers on that side through the K1 enable relay. Public 46 drives the right pair and 48 the left pair; 45/47 repeat the synthetic state. Matrix 32 is the separate right-button lane-change contact. Each assembly has a physical EOS contact for its dual-winding coil, but this driver publishes no independent EOS input or upper-flipper output.
mechanisms.label: Four hard-wired flippers

All three retained ROM runs publish a startup burst at outputs 17-20; the exact rising and falling edges remain recorded as observations. The PIA writes or ROM initialization causing that burst have not been established. Inverted PIA transport and startup timing alone do not explain its cause, so availability remains unknown. The not-applicable spatial record describes documented physical non-fitment; it does not resolve the published state.

It enables all four flippers; it is not an upper-right flipper output.
